A number with a unit

Source: R/units.R
u.Rd

u(value, unit) makes a units value. The unit is taken as written and never evaluated as R: u(35, m), u(5, mg/L), u(1, m^2); or it is a string, u(150, "CFU/100 mL"). value is a numeric vector, or a units value, which is converted: u(dict$core_len, cm).

Usage

u(value, unit)

Arguments

value

A numeric vector or a units value.

unit

A unit expression, written as it is, or a string.

Value

A units value.

Details

A unit held in a variable cannot be given to u(), which takes it as written; do.call(u, list(3, "m")) does that, and so does units::set_units(x, un, mode = "standard"). u() makes a quantity, and weft cannot stop base R's %in%, match(), cut() and findInterval() from comparing one with a bare number, as they work on the bare numbers (rule 4.4.5 is kept by claim() and the comparison operators only).

u() registers no unit of its own. The first time weft parses or converts a unit in a session, and each time a configuration is read, it brings the units database to weft's default table (see unit_defaults(): pH, mph, nmi, Ma, ka, gal, NTU, PSU, CFU, MPN, and names for ppm and ppb) and the project's units: rows (rules 4.4.21, 9.1.7); loading weft changes nothing. A unit the units database does not know is a weft_unit_error; a project's own unit is registered when the dictionary that names it is read (rule 4.4.7), or with units::install_unit(). A unit that does not convert, a value that is not numeric and a missing unit are a weft_unit_error too.

A unit is kept as written: u(2, Sv) holds Sv, not the Gy the units package substitutes, and weft refuses to convert between units the database defines alike (Sv, Gy and rem; Bq, Hz and Ci; VA and W; and Hz or Bq and an angle per time such as rpm), in of_n(), about() and a claim() comparison as in a conversion; arithmetic is left to units. Under unit_defaults: weft (the default in _weft.yml) a unit the units package reads as a prefix and another unit that a report does not mean (mt as a millitonne, kt as a knot, kph as a kilophot) is a weft_unit_error whose message says what it was read as and what to write; under unit_defaults: si it is read as the units package reads it (rule 4.4.20).

u(NA, mm) is a missing quantity and u(logical(0), mm) an empty one; TRUE and FALSE are refused. Inside a compound unit each token is kept as typed and prints as typed (mm/hr prints mm/hr, rule 4.4.20). grade is refused like mt: the units package reads it as an angle; name a project unit in units: instead. A bare quantity in prose (`r u(3, mm)` with no class) prints as stock knitr prints it and raises a weft_unit_warning; add {.num} or {.nounit}. The same warning is raised when the prose after a printed quantity types its unit again.

Examples

u(35, m)
#> 35 [m]
u(5, mg/L)
#> 5 [mg/L]
